decisions.quote: This shows that this cooling effect requires a specific experimental procedure and is thus not strictly `psychologically induced’ by the subjective RHI and the consequent experienced disownership of one’s real hand, as proposed in [ 2 ]. We observe both, a subjective ownership illusion without cooling (Experiment 1 and 2) and a cooling of the stimulated hand independent of subjectively felt ownership (Experiment 3 control). The relative cooling only occurs in the manual stroking procedure (Experiment 3) and is independent of the subjective ownership illusion.
decisions.reason: Moseley et al. (2008) claimed that illusory ownership in the RHI psychologically induces relative cooling of the stimulated hand (supported by a condition x hand interaction and a correlation with ownership vividness). Across three experiments, Rohde et al. (2013) found no cooling at all in Experiments 1 and 2 despite strong ownership illusions, and in Experiment 3 (manual stroking) found relative cooling of the stimulated hand in both the experimental and control conditions (no significant condition x hand interaction, p = 0.103; no main effect of condition, p = 0.272) and no correlation with ownership vividness in any experiment. Because even Experiment 3 failed to reproduce an RHI-specific cooling effect or a correlation with ownership, the study is not 'statistically successful but flawed', nor is it 'mixed': the authors' overall verdict is that the three experiments demonstrate a double dissociation refuting Moseley et al.'s claim that hand cooling is a strict, psychologically induced correlate of subjective hand ownership in the RHI.

decisions.quote: We set out to replicate the psychologically induced cooling of the stimulated hand during the RHI reported by Moseley et al. [ 2 ] in three consecutive experiments, comparing different experimental procedures. While we could not replicate the results at all with the automated stroking procedure (used in [ 13 ]), it was possible to replicate the result using a manual stroking procedure, albeit in both the experimental and the control condition.
decisions.reason: Across three experiments re-testing Moseley et al. (2008), the authors explicitly state that they could not replicate the cooling effect in the automated stroking procedures (Experiments 1 and 2) but replicated relative cooling of the stimulated hand using the manual stroking procedure (Experiment 3), albeit in both the experimental and control conditions and without the original correlation with ownership vividness.

scope_review.parent_objection: First reply calls the three experiments mixed: no cooling with automated stroking,but manual-stroking cooling in both illusion and control conditions. Discussion then explicitly says cooling is independent of subjective ownership,requires a specific procedure,and is not strictly psychologically induced by the RHI as proposed by Moseley2008. Determine whether the paper main message is a methodological/construct-validity critique warranting statistically successful but flawed after recovering cooling,an overall failed test of the original ownership-specific causal claim,or an actual mixed verdict. Do not equate any hand cooling with replication of psychologically induced cooling,or infer category solely from counts of experiments. Follow authors own overall verdict and main-message scope; inspect full abstract,Discussion,and conclusion. Type and Moseley2008 identity remain settled.
